Why the plate corner broke off

NACS wall holder, the print of September 19, dropped on the floor on October 10. Both pictures come from the real print file (the revision uses the same plate, pads and slicer recipe), not from a sketch.

The base plate is 3/16 in thick, but it is not solid. The slicer prints it as two skins of three layers (about 1/32 in each) over a 20% gyroid core, with three walls around the edge. The only solid plastic is the pad around each screw, 1/2 in in radius. Everything else inside the plate is open lattice, so a corner that hits the floor is a thin hollow flap with a half-depth countersink through it.

The numbers

FeatureAs printedWhy it matters
Plate thickness3/16 inTwo 1/32 in skins carry all the bending; the core only spaces them
Core between the skins20% gyroid, 1/8 in thickShears and crushes under a corner hit; a break face here looks hollow
Walls at the plate edge3 loops, about 5/64 inThe only solid plastic along the edge outside the pads
Solid pad around each screw1/2 in radiusProtects the ring around the hole, not the flap's root along the edge (about 7/8 in of edge per corner is unprotected)
Countersink3/32 in deep, half the plateHalves the section at the hole, and the drum blend lands on its edge
Material and layersPETG Basic, 0.30 mm layers, plate downLayers lie in the plate's plane; a drop bends the corner across them, which the skins resist well but the lattice does not

What that means

A drop onto a corner puts the whole holder's momentum into one flap of plate. The two thin skins have to take the bending on their own, with a half-depth countersink and the drum's blend both landing on the same line. Once the skins crack, the lattice core has nothing to offer, so the corner comes away clean. The screw pads kept the ring around the hole solid, and nothing else.

One question before I draw the fix: where did it break?
  1. A crescent outside the screw hole came off and the hole is half gone (the break ran through the hole).
  2. The whole corner, hole included, came off along the drum (the break ran around the drum's blend).
A photo of the break face would settle it, and show whether the core looks hollow.

Where this points

  • Make the plate solid. A 100% infill modifier over the whole plate, no CAD change. Roughly 40 g and 25 to 30 min more on the revision print, to be confirmed by a slice. This is the cheapest change and fixes the hollow core in every corner.
  • Thicken the plate. 1/4 in instead of 3/16 in gives the countersink a full plate under it and moves the drum blend off the countersink's edge. The drum and everything on it move out 1/16 in, so the CAD exports, the docking check and the slice rerun.
  • Both together is the belt and braces version. Either way the revision stays unprinted until you pick.
